purpose: The animal's equivalent of ORGAN_GREEN_LEDGER.json. One record per learning faculty, judged against LC1..LC12 by scripts/verify_learning_conditions.py. Verdicts are COMPUTED, never written here by hand: this file declares the inputs (owner, entrypoints, callers, stores, tests, evidence) and the verifier decides. A faculty is green only when every condition passes or is declared N/A-BY-DESIGN with a referent.
honesty_note: The first honest run of this ledger is expected to be mostly yellow. A ledger that goes green on the day it is written is not measuring anything.

ORGANIC, and the first time this link has ever fired on real code. Run 20260921T220054-16cdf659 against the self-corpus pinned at 613f9332: a read+verify task over this repository's own tests/test_code_chunking.py earned three STRONG turns (3 passed each), the arc verified, the cerebellum compiled it (playbook 15), and the next request for that goal was served with the LLM client rigged to raise if consulted -- llm_calls=0, events ended cerebellum_done. The playbook cited is one THIS run earned: `_organic_playbook` refuses to count the newest compiled playbook, because an earlier check did exactly that and lit up on a leftover synthetic seed.
live_evidence.note: Two runs before this one reported passed=False strength=NONE and looked like a model failing. They were the harness: the scope cwd is the scope root's PARENT, so `pytest -k ...` collected the home directory and returned a pytest INTERNALERROR. The same selection run in the corpus is `3 passed in 10s`. A failing measurement is not a failing subject -- checked first, as L8 requires.

discharged_blockers.blocker: (1) WRITE-CONFIRM. A self-corpus pin arc contains a `create_file` step. A replay may only CONFIRM such a step when the exact bytes were approved by a human (`playbook_blobs` via `aios/core/replay_writes.py::load_content`). The self-corpus has no human, and registering agent-written bytes as approved would be forging an approval.
discharged_blockers.discharged_by: Not discharged -- ROUTED AROUND. A pin arc still cannot be replayed, and that guard is correct: registering agent-written bytes as human-approved would be forging an approval. The verify-only arc has no create_file step, so the guard never applies rather than being weakened. `playbook_blobs` and `replay_writes.load_content` are untouched.

discharged_blockers.blocker: (2) APPROVAL GATE. The write-free alternative -- a read+verify arc over a real module -- is blocked at the gateway: `pytest` is on the YELLOW (approval-required) list, and the auto-execute allowlist is `echo` and `pwd` only. An unattended training run has no approver, so the verify never executes. Observed directly: `tool_blocked` on `pytest tests/test_code_chunking.py` inside the corpus.
discharged_blockers.discharged_by: Operator granted the scoped approval on 2026-09-22 (asked for by name in this ledger's previous revision). The harness now holds ONE exact command string for the duration of one run: not a prefix, not a pattern, nothing written to config. The gateway is unchanged -- `pytest` stays YELLOW for everyone else, which tests/test_training_approval_is_narrow.py::TestTheGatewayItselfIsUnchanged fails if anyone reclassifies it. Approval still cannot buy RED (execute_approved re-evaluates) and the scope lock still confines the command to the throwaway worktree; both directions are asserted in that file.

journal.claim: Mastery fires once per level by construction, which is exactly why it needs journalling: the UPDATE that records it destroys when and by which run it happened.

mutation_probe.claim: Breaking `_refresh_level` so it never promotes must stop any mastery signal reaching `on_mastered`; if one still arrives, the signal comes from somewhere other than the thing that decides mastery.

live_evidence.description: ORGANIC, and stated as two separate claims because they are two separate claims. (1) PROGRESSION ON REAL CODE: run 20260921T222322-e4a34769 against the self-corpus pinned at aaa95d00 mastered `gagos-real-modules` level 1 -- two training passes and one held-out pass, every one STRONG, on real corpus suites proven green before they were used as tasks. The production CurriculumManager decided mastery; nothing in the harness decides what 'enough' is. (2) MINING REAL CODE: the same run's CurriculumMiner read this run's own pin attempts and proposed `Read aios/agents/tool_agent.py and then create tests/test_tool_agent_pinned_v2.py ...` -- a real module, which was structurally impossible before.
live_evidence.scope_note: WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the mined proposal was NOT executed, and nothing accepted it. Accepting a mined proposal into the curriculum is the one act the miner must never perform for itself, and a training harness performing it on the miner's behalf is the same act wearing a different hat. The level's tasks were authored by the harness over real corpus modules -- as curriculum tasks always are -- and lived in a RUN-SCOPED database, so the real curriculum is untouched by this evidence.

discharged_blockers.blocker: CurriculumMiner is now called from the live turn path (fail-open, default-on, ~90ms), so proposals are generated without anyone asking. But `_extract_module_name` matches `training_ground/<name>.py` and NOTHING else, and every escalation template describes creating a toy module -- so the miner structurally cannot propose from work on real code. LC10 is therefore unreachable for L6 until the miner is redesigned around real repositories, which is a design project rather than a regex change. Pinned by tests/test_curriculum_mining_is_live.py::test_it_can_only_mine_the_TOY_world.
discharged_blockers.discharged_by: A real-code escalation family (`pin_real_behaviour`), selected by the TARGET being real rather than by the source prompt's verb. `_extract_module_name` is deliberately unchanged: the toy templates interpolate into a `training_ground/...` path, so widening the extractor alone would have pointed toy templates at real files. Proposals also LEAVE the process now (.aios/audit/curriculum-proposals.jsonl, accepted=false) -- what used to leave was a log line counting them, so the authority boundary the miner protects had nothing on the other side of it to accept. tests/test_curriculum_mining_is_live.py carries the positive assertions AND the negative control that the toy world still mines the toy way.
